a series of 1-alkyl-2-phenyl-substituted 4-quinolone derivatives have been synthesized and found to be potent cytotoxic agents and inhibitors of tubulin assembly.

1,6-substituted-2-phenylquinolones are potent antimitotic agents that inhibit tubulin polymerization and that 2-(4-phenylphenyl)-4- quinolones with substituents at C-6 and C-7 are potent inhibitors of tubulins binding to colchicine.

the design and synthesis of novel antimitotic agents based on the 2-phenyquinolone structure, and we have identified several compounds that inhibit tubulin polymerization and are cytotoxic to human tumor cell lines.

the design of antitumor agents that interact with tubulin and the discovery of novel antimitotic agents that inhibit tubulin polymerization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1,6-7,8-substitution of 2-(4-substituted phenyl)quinolones is a viable approach to the design of potent cytotoxic compounds that inhibit tubulin polymerization.

the 1,6- and 1,7-disubstituted 2-aryl-4-quinones (22-26 and 28-30) are potent antimitotic agents that inhibit tubulin polymerization and colchicine binding to tubulin.

the 2-pheny-4-quinolinone ring system is a useful scaffold for the design of new antimitotic agents that inhibit tubulin polymerization.
the 2-pheny-4-quinoline scaffold is an excellent platform for the development of antimitotic agents that interact with tubulin.
